notes.title: PLAYTEST BEGINS! To all squads: arm up!
notes.content:
[p][b]Squad Commanders,[/b]
[/p][p]This is not a drill. A new transmission has come from Luxorix HQ:[/p][code] >URGENT. PLAYTEST IS OUT. ALL SQUADS TO DEPLOY. [/code][previewyoutube="mIs2yiGq0rQ;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]A number of changes have been made to both synth and environment systems. Make preparations and get ready for:[/p][list][*][p][b]New Energy System.[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]Each squad member now has access to multiple skills that require smart selection, tactical timing and strategic use of energy. Take advantage of this flexibility in combat to discover the full potential of your squad.[/p][list][*][p][b]Reworked Metaprogression.[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]This time, it’s all about variety: new weapons, implants, and skills. As commander, it’s your duty to lead the squad as effectively as possible. Adapt, experiment and exploit every option to unlock wild synergies and build loadouts even we didn’t see coming. Pressure either breaks or makes humans stronger. Synths? They only [i]thrive[/i] under pressure.[/p][list][*][p][b]Redesigned Camp System.[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]Rest stops are no longer just for patching wounds or occasionally grilling a steak. Now, your pool of available activities depends on who’s in your squad. Bring different heroes to unlock all options. Choose wisely, so every stop counts.

[/p][p]All of these changes were made to enhance replayability offering a broader range of variety, and improve the progression system. What do you think? How does it feel? [/p][p]Drop your feedback and suggestions here:[url="https://forms.gle/VwWFz9YtP1Vvggbn9"] [/url][/p][p][url="https://forms.gle/VwWFz9YtP1Vvggbn9"]https://forms.gle/VwWFz9YtP1Vvggbn9[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Want to chat with us directly or converse with fellow commanders? Deploy to our Discord, the comms are open. Let’s talk.
[/p][p][i]Over and Out,[/i][/p][p][i]Luxorix and Critical Reflex[/i][/p][p]

notes.title: The Safest Haven
notes.content:
[h1]Welcome back to the Station![/h1]

Today we’re going to take a little breather between the long and dangerous raids. Your synths need time to recuperate and strengthen their morale. The best way to do that is to take time spending your hard earned resources on upgrades. Let’s take a look at the main buildings of the station.

[h2]MAIN SERVER[/h2]
The mysterious Professor is always working on something in the name of greater good. At least, as far as he claims it to be. Whatever his true intentions are, we are lucky to have him on our side. His deep connections to slavers and traders of the Wasteland, as well as intrinsic understanding of what makes all synths tick, makes his inventions a huge help in our line of work.

[h2]TRAIN-FACTORY[/h2]
First comes the distant rumble, then the rhythmic clicking, ending in the heavy hiss of brakes. Yes, finally the long-awaited train arrived. Once a means of transport, now it’s a top-notch factory that is capable of enhancing your synths’ unique abilities. However, whenever you get something, you have to give back. Some modules come with slight drawbacks, so make sure to read through thoroughly.

[h2]LABORATORY[/h2]
Lab techs give out their best in an effort to create implants that provide better chances of survival during the raids. Given that there are only eight available spaces for each of the heroes, make sure that the implants provide the best advantage to each of them. Don’t forget to use all opportunities to get the implants during the raids, to make sure your synths are at their best.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]MEET THE SQUAD[/h2]
When things are heating up, we need all the reinforcements we can get. Bastion and Viper are one of the core members, each bringing their own unique approach to survival. Let’s meet them.

[h2]Bastion[/h2]
Sometimes you hear him mutter something to himself. The only word you can discern is “Legion”. The scars on his face, the unabated will to protect as if he has taken a solemn vow… Something dark must have happened to him before he ended up at the Station. You can’t help yourself but wonder what.
Bastion, just as his name suggests, is a walking fortress, built to take in any attack. With his massive shield and top-tier armor, Bastion is the toughest tank out there. He’s slow and doesn’t hit as hard as others, but his ability to soak up damage makes him an irreplaceable frontline.

With the right upgrades, he becomes a wrecking ball in melee combat, overwhelming enemies with sheer force.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/rfwLtN4.gif[/img]

[h2]Viper[/h2]
Once a mercenary working for the Bureau, Viper seems to still have some ties to her past. Maybe, if you spend enough time together, she’ll be ready to open up.

Where she might lack power, she easily compensates with lethal precision. Viper thrives on long-range combat, taking down threats before they even get close. She’s fragile, but her exceptional range allows her to stay behind the frontlines, picking off enemies with deadly accuracy.

She [i]can[/i] fight up close if needed, but keeping her at a distance is the best way to play to her strengths.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/2d3VkOp.gif[/img]
[hr][/hr]
We’ll provide more information on buildings that are supported by Fractions next time. The politics are never-ending even after a collapse of the society we once knew. It is vital to know who to trust and what you can gain from working with others.

Another bit of information to everyone interested to be [i]the first[/i] to explore all the changes in Deadlock Station: click [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2327640/Deadlock_Station/]Request Access[/url] on the game page to get a chance to join the closed beta playtest.

End of transmission.[hr][/hr]
[i]Over and out,
Luxorix and Critical Reflex.[/i]

notes.title: Updated Demo is Available!
notes.content:
[h3]Attention Station residents![/h3]

The time has come! The Station was in power-saving mode for too long. It is time once again to dust off the guns, grease the hinges and march out into the reaches unknown – the alien invasion won’t stop itself. 

[b]For this Next Fest we’ve rolled out an updated demo of the game![/b] Featuring new mechanics, content and new enemy balance, brushed up and refreshed. Several systems were reworked completely, resulting in new in-raid and meta progression, and new enemies and hazards were added. [i]It’ll keep you on your toes even if you played the previous demo.[/i]

[b]There’s plenty of new stuff:[/b]

[list]
[*] [b]Brand new system of implants and modules.[/b] Some of them are universal and some are unique to squad members, drastically changing their abilities and encouraging new playstyles
[*] [b]Reworked starter sets.[/b] Now instead of a set list of consumables, you get randomized starting equipment, now the set is different for every run. 
[*] [b]Dozens of new equipment items with not just stats,[/b] but also special properties allowing to create unique character builds.
[*] [b]Completely new look on the Ferals.[/b] You’ve met them in the previous demo, but now they're a full enemy faction armed with acidic weapons (yes, guns too). Dangerous like never before.
[*] [b]New level types and new interactable objects on the battlefield.[/b] Throwers tossing enemies back and forth, transmitters summoning backup, weather conditions and ground elevations to really expand on your positioning.
[/list] 

The demo is [b]already available[/b], so don’t keep the New Earth waiting – try it out and, of course, add Deadlock Station to your wishlist! It’ll be much appreciated.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2327640/Deadlock_Station/

And feel free to share your thoughts about the game! Join CRITICAL REFLEX discord server.

notes.title: Urban Dangers
notes.content:
[h3]Attention Station residents! [/h3]

Long time no see! It’s time for another devlog. Today, as promised, we’re going to peek into the Black City, wander its labyrinths made of asphalt, metal and concrete. Maybe even watch some synths doing stuff they always do — swim in pools of acid and occasionally get electrocuted. But at least we’ll meet some new faces along the way!

However, your righteous crusade to the Black City is bound to have obstacles. The first one is the Concrete Jungle that needs some… pest control.

[h2]The Concrete Jungle[/h2]

Outskirts of the city only seem to look abandoned: with its improvised tire barricades and dismantled cars, all covered with an even layer of dust and garbage. Of course its inhabitants are not the most welcoming type. You’re already familiar with the Ravagers from the previous devlog and even met them in our Demo. These desperate synths are scavenging for leftover tech and supplies — and they don’t care to share. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/78XiR0e.gif[/img]

And don’t forget the safety hazards scattered everywhere: exposed wires, unstable constructions and suspiciously open sewage hatches. Although these are more dangerous to your enemies, rather than your heroes.

For example, there are some barrels still waiting for proper transportation. Naturally, you can safely [i]“transport”[/i] them on your enemies’ heads. There’s even a convenient lever to ensure the barrels reach their unlucky recipient.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/SrWLANN.gif[/img]

Another piece of environment that could help you on your crusade to the alien ship is the city’s power grid. Or rather its poor condition. One careless step (or rather one carefully calculated knockback) – and the whole enemy squad gets electrocuted. Of course this can happen to you too, but we believe in your tactical skills.  

[img]https://i.imgur.com/6jIH5CS.gif[/img]

The only thing more numerous than traps — are the rats, crawling in the sewage system. We’re talking endless swarm of pests with a complete absence of fear or even self-preservation instinct. Don’t even try to clear the place, just thin their ranks enough to escape and move on. You try closing  the sewage hatches to control the side they’re coming from. But this won’t hold them for long.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/h8Jtnnt.gif[/img]

According to our intel, something is controlling these rats. They seem to have some kind of a leader. We are unsure of its origin and can’t share much information about it… yet.  Discovering the source of rat infestation and eliminating it is [b]your[/b] task. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/yIt9fgp.png[/img]

[h2]The Black City[/h2]

The Black City used to be a blooming metropolis: clean streets, automation everywhere, order and safety. Even waste recycling! Real humans wandered its streets and supercomputers were calculating the most efficient pipelines for practically everything. It was an urban paradise… 

[i][b]“Was”[/b][/i] is the key word here. Now that it’s abandoned — this is one of the worst places on New Earth. It’s all-concrete walls, acid pools and well-armed renegades. Tread cautiously, because some conveyor belts and disposal mechanisms are still working. And you don’t want to be disposed of, do you? Thanks to conveniently placed switches, you at least can turn the conveyors off. But then you can’t push an enemy into a grinder… and where’s the fun in that?

[img]https://i.imgur.com/PwhlD5C.gif[/img]

There are also mobile multi-purpose units scattered around. We call them Sarcophagi for convenience. Some were used for heating, some — for transporting acid. They are beyond repair, but still can be useful in a fight. Since they’re mobile, you can push them, creating a makeshift barricade. Or just flatten the enemy with them. These can break though, be careful. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/mEFpD8u.gif[/img]

If you happen to get through Renegade scouts to the center of the city, you can’t avoid the pinnacle of pre-disaster robotics — The Grossmeister. However, reports indicate that, despite its name, it can no longer be reasoned with. Shoot on sight, and avoid standing on drainages. It’s your best chance. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/zIELWUv.png[/img]

[h2]New Faces on the Station[/h2]

This briefing was pretty demoralizing. Enemies, hazards, rats and acid… We should have some good news for a change. The Station just got reinforcements! New heroes are ready to take on every enemy out there. Let’s take a closer look.

[h3]Pathfinder[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/2yRcK90.png[/img]

Long-range specialist armed with a high-caliber sniper rifle and a knife for occasional hand-to-hand combat. 

[i]He’s all about the distance.[/i] While his fire rate is comparably slow, the damage is high enough to one-shot smaller enemies. But his main strength is surviving without ever taking hits. His special ability allows him to teleport away from enemies, leaving behind a hologram to confuse the attackers. 

Pathfinder is quite frail, but, if all cards were played right, can eliminate multiple enemies singlehandedly. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Oe5eYM2.gif[/img]

[h3]Warden[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/OkJJpuF.png[/img]

Now this one can and will take a hit, it’s his main strategy. He was built that way. Sure, he isn’t nimble at all, but he also doesn’t have to approach you to show his affinity with cold weapons. He has drones. And these drones stun and drag enemies closer. 

He also has an intimidating aura. That’s not really a fighting skill, he’s just scary.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/vd0dUVB.gif[/img]

This marks the end of this devlog. As you see, New Earth is full of dangers, and it is your solemn duty to cleanse it, capture the alien ship and restore order. May you return to the Station safely.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2327640/Deadlock_Station/

notes.title: Know Your Enemy
notes.content:
[h3]Attention station residents![/h3]

[b]New Earth is a dangerous place:[/b] it hasn’t seen peace ever since humanity fell. Gangs, cults and factions constantly fight for their place under the sun. Many synths are standing between you and the alien ship. So in this devlog we’re going to prepare you for the awaiting dangers. Let’s have a little briefing on things you’ll have to fight.

[b]Without further ado, let’s talk about enemies![/b]

[h2]Ravagers[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43690858/de67be5d628f67137dd1323208cef3225e055b6e.png[/img]

Aggressive bandits, raiding everything and mugging everyone. Despite their deeds, they pursue a very relatable goal. All their actions are aimed at the most basic goal – [i]survival[/i]. 

They live under the constant fear of [i]“death”[/i]: deactivation, malfunctioning or running out of power. This dictates their never-ending search for batteries and spare parts.

[b]Although, not all of them are violent maniacs.[/b] Some Ravagers are willing to  trade with you in exchange for energy. Keep in mind though — they are always desperate enough to attack you, if their deal doesn’t go as planned.

[img]https://i.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExMTF6bmxnOHIyZ3U1ZGtobjBzM2I1Nm95NGlrcG96bTlkMXFwZWFxdCZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/UvfzONigWVMplBJ0TZ/source.gif[/img]

One can’t say they’re heavily armed. [i]Or at least not consistently so.[/i] Their weaponry usually consists of  what they could scavenge on the battlefield. [b]Sometimes it’s a plank with nails, sometimes – military-grade equipment.[/b]

[img]https://i.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExNm0wZ2s5YnJ4b2htZnAzbnA2eThsMzY2dW03Z2JtdXFvamM1NW0wbiZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/Ye3H1u86ZBXjrwDcHO/source.gif[/img]

Regardless of what they have on hand, they still pose a real threat to your team. Some of them carry the artillery that flies over obstacles. And some just hit so hard — it knocks your heroes back into an adjacent battlefield.

[h2]Ferals[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43690858/8229322609a8ec3102799ad9378aa58ea3cd961b.png[/img]

[b]Some of the synths wandering New Earth stick to a more primal way of life – calling themselves the Ferals.[/b] Instead of choosing leaders or common goals, they seem to have developed a religious cult. And not the welcoming type. 

From what little bits of information we have, it can be assumed that they worship “the Beast”. Getting more details about their cult proves difficult, since Ferals aren’t the talkative bunch.

[b]Whatever their goals may be, they turn them into selfless zealots — and a huge threat.[/b] To minimize losses, better plan your positioning thoroughly. Ambush is one of their favorite tactics. Exercise caution near big garbage piles.

[img]https://i.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExaGxoNmNzN3V6NGFqZTBnMW91a3lvbGh1eWplNzhzNHRsc2k2NG5xeiZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/1M82vFt4AcP9QPfQ24/source.gif[/img]

Most of them are incapable of ranged combat, but excel at hand-to-hand fighting, helped by their talons, which leave puddles of acid with every strike. It’s generally a bad idea to stand in something as corrosive, so [b]you should try to keep your distance when engaging with the Ferals.
[/b]
[h2]Renegades[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43690858/3824c19567c17c0dff3a7eedf43be185884940ba.png[/img]

[b]Probably the most dangerous synths encountered so far.[/b] Unlike other factions, they are unified  by a common goal. As Dr. Isaacson theorises, the Renegades might have established contact with the aliens and are helping with their invasion. 

Compared to other synths roaming the New Earth, the Renegades seem to be the most organized group, [b]using advanced battle tactics and deploying a lot of specialized units.[/b] Equipped with everything from shotguns and sniper rifles to stun batons and grenade launchers — they seem prepared to face off any opponent.

[b]In most battles their marksmen provide covering fire for their frontline, so your best bet is flanking or breaking their formation[/b]

[img]https://i.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExMm02b3JnYjJueXVkOTZ6Y3hyemRqd2cwdm5xM3A3Y3hsdnZwMWt0MCZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/uYgnpoSCxb9FkIbT2S/source.gif[/img]

[h2]Awaiting dangers[/h2]

[b]When roaming the wasteland don’t expect to run only into synths.[/b] Wildlife can be just as dangerous. And with the humanity fallen, there is a resurgence of it — so expect to be outnumbered. 

[b]Spiders from lairs around the station have developed a weird defensive mechanism — exploding violently on death.[/b] Apparently, some of them sacrifice themselves to preserve the lair. If you don’t want a dying spider to take your arm with it, better keep your distance. There are several efficient strategies: repelling artifacts, AoE specials and flanking their nests. 

[img]https://i.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExMHA4aWppOGVqNXh0MXV4YmcwejlydXZ5YnAwNmxuYzA2eDZpeXRwbyZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/mfBc0zC1NnDg9Oz8ya/source.gif[/img]

[b]And while swamps are swarmed with spiders, rats occupy the city sewers.[/b] Without pest control[i] (or any control, frankly speaking)[/i] they grew in size, numbers and courage. Enough to attack surface dwellers by forming big swarms. They are still pretty disorganized, but there are a lot of them. If you don’t find the life of a Swiss cheese exactly thrilling — do your best to dispatch of them quickly.

[img]https://i.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExbWJ2a3plM2lnazA0cWk3dGZ6bDFmNWFuMjBscWNoeW5oOXZrZTRsaSZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/Nmacvm4aJuDKK4np2P/source.gif[/img]

[b]Our intel also reports sightings of another synth faction farther into the city.[/b] Little is known about them apart from their [i]unconventional way of producing and storing energy[/i]. We will share any findings in the future updates. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43690858/418aef705587358c90f2460b6f02806706946d2c.png[/img]

As you can see, New Earth’s inhabitants mostly aren’t willing to help the cause. This only makes your mission more heroic – you’re defying the odds! So don’t let this stop your march to the alien ship. In our next briefing we are going to talk about the Black City and what awaits you in its abandoned streets.

[b]Ironhive[/b] is a deck-building strategy game in which you try to preserve the last human settlement in the barren post-apocalyptic world.  After raiding the outer world from the station, protecting the station itself from the horrors outside should feel refreshing. 
[b]Try it for yourself in the free demo!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43690858/c122b4f363f5600746f25bc719e58b054b988d29.png[/img]

This marks the end of our briefing. We hope it provided useful information and somewhat satisfied your hunger for knowledge. Send us your questions and feedback, it’ll help us make the game even better.

notes.title: Deadlock Station Demo Coming to Steam July 29th!
notes.content:
[h3]Hello everyone![/h3]

You’ve seen screenshots, trailers, but today we can finally show you the real thing! After all, screenshots can’t show our game in full bloom. So, without further ado…

[h2]Deadlock Station demo is coming out July 29th! [/h2]

[h3]Featuring:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]4 available characters[/b] to build your team  —  a heavily armed [b]Executioner[/b], far-reaching [b]Gunner[/b], frail but exceptionally strong [b]Raider[/b] and an impenetrable [b]Legionary[/b]!
[*] [b]Various quests[/b] with run-altering outcomes. Every choice counts!
[*] [b]A new twist on the system of random events[/b] with different outcomes depending on your choices. Every choice counts, so make the out of what you get!
[*] [b]Meta-progression[/b] with upgrades and unlockable items  — die, upgrade, repeat!
[*] [b]А big boss-fight in the end — it’s giant, it’s evil, it’s challenging, but we believe you will prevail[/b]
[/list]

notes.title: Devlog: resources and inventory
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Today's devlog will begin with a description of the resources. At the moment there are 2 main resources in the game: ether and sulfur.

[h3]Ether[/h3]

Ether is an organic substance that is extracted from dead Aliens. It is a very valuable resource because it is used to make mutagen. This resource is used as currency by traders and slave traders, so if you want to replenish your supplies or squad strength, you can't do without ether.

[h3]Sulfur[/h3]

Sulfur, are pieces of meteorite ore of yellow color. This is why it is popularly called "sulfur". Sulfur is used to make weapons and as a source of energy. It is also required for the operation of alien mechanisms, which is why Aliens fight fiercely for this resource.

Sulfur is mined with drills. You set the auger before each battle and, at the end of the battle, the auger adds up the amount of sulphur you've extracted. The work of the drill attracts the attention of enemies and they try to destroy it, so it always requires protection. There is almost no sulfur around the station, so the more levels you pass, the further away from the station you are, the more sulfur your drills mine.

Sulfur is only used at the station to unlock new items, weapons and armor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43690858/d56e31bf8ce6cbbd651248f9f104242d4c38a898.gif[/img]

[h3]Inventory[/h3]

Each hero has 3 different slots and you can put into them only those items that fit the chosen hero.

[list]
[*] [b]The first slot is used for weapons.[/b] In addition to the fact that the weapon increases the melee or ranged damage of the hero, it can also give a unique buff. By combining the weapon buff with the hero's mutations, you can get quite strong synergies.
[*] [b]The second slot is used for armor.[/b] The game has light and heavy armor, and each hero can wear only one of the options.
[*] [b]The third slot is used for items.[/b] The game has many different gizmos that can be put in this slot, ranging from shoes to a healing kit that resurrects the hero after a death.
[/list]
The squad's inventory is common to all heroes. But as we said above, not all items fit the chosen fighter. For example, in the screenshot below you can see that there is a gun in the inventory, but it is dark because it does not fit the Legionnaire. However, there is an arrow above the Rifleman in the squad, which indicates that this gun will fit him, and the green color suggests that the new gun will be better than the equipped one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43690858/a86699335bc928c0f04c05064552da9adc058825.png[/img]
Some items in your inventory, such as food, medicine and mutagen, are instantaneous and do not need slots. They are just consumables and are activated by pressing.

That's all for now. Next time we'll talk about mutagen and mutations.

notes.title: Devlog: About the game and future plans
notes.content:
Hello, everyone!

The last few months have been very busy. Our team finished the demo after 14 months of development. We showed the demo to a small group of testers on our [url=https://discord.gg/mCWh9445qN]discord[/url] and after fixing the bugs we sent it out to publishers.

We still have a lot of work ahead of us, because the demo has about 30% of the planned content. We are also continuing to feel the optimal balance of difficulty and resources.

[h3]Deadlock Station World[/h3]

Earth has been invaded by Aliens. Why did they invade? Where did they come from? The answers to these questions will be revealed as we go along. All we know at the beginning is that humanity survived the catastrophe and is now surviving in a half-destroyed world while fighting the Aliens.

The starting point of each race is a train station, which is located on the edge of the wasteland. Looters (artifact hunters) travel there by train, form into squads, buy ammunition and head out into the wasteland in search of valuable resources and to hunt down Aliens.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43690858/bf4261bdf9ff47add339ec7488257195fc59e2cf.png[/img]

Due to anomalies in the wasteland electronics do not work, so looters use time-tested powder, diesel and hydraulic weapons, as well as crossbows, knives, bludgeons, etc.

After each sortie we get resources that can be spent at the station, unlocking new items, weapons, armor, mutations, as well as starter kits. All of this will help make the next sorties more effective.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43690858/6d5de405c572503df90c53d8c10d022eb79df4ab.png[/img]

We'll talk more about resources, anomalies, and ammunition in the next devlogs.
